title: On Retiring from the school at sixty
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：retire　|　正文 352 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 retire 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the trader ① retired from the school at sixty on the same day, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the trader ② retires from the school at sixty before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ retire from the school at sixty at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ retired from the school at sixty before — a line in the list for October 1955 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Retiring from the school at sixty on the same day, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ retire to the far room after supper before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Retire to the far room after supper at once and never mention it again.

By 1968 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new partner from the next market ⑧ retires to the far room after supper on the same day every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ retired from the school at sixty again when nobody else would.

⑩ To retire from the school at sixty, my mother said in 1973, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the market remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the market forgets, somebody retires from the school at sixty before dawn again and somebody must retire from the school at sixty on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 退休（一般过去式 retired from the school at sixty：1961 年货商头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 退休（一般现在 retires from the school at sixty：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 退休（不定式 to retire from the school at sixty：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 退休（过去完成时 had retired from the school at sixty：1955 年十月的货单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 退休（动名词 retiring from the school at sixty 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 退下（retire to the far room after supper：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去退下晚饭后退进最里那间屋）
G. v. 退下（retire to the far room after supper：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 退休（后段两处：新来的伙计照例 retires to the far room after supper，而母亲又一次 retired from the school at sixty）

answers.why: retire 意为“退休”，1961 年货商当天就退休六十岁从学堂退下来，那是集市里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 retired。
retire 意为“退休”，自那以后货商天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 retires。
retire 意为“退休”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯退休六十岁从学堂退下来”，此处为不定式 to retire from the school at sixty。
retire 意为“退休”，货单里 十月 那行字说明早在 1968 年之前就有人退休过，故用过去完成时 had retired。
retire 意为“退休”，货商说“退休六十岁从学堂退下来这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 retiring from the school at sixty 作主语。
retire 意为“退下”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去退下晚饭后退进最里那间屋”，should ever 之后用原形 retire to the far room after supper。
retire 意为“退下”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻退下晚饭后退进最里那间屋（retire to the far room after supper at once），以后再也不要提起。
retire 意为“退休”，新来的伙计每个星期都照例退下晚饭后退进最里那间屋，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 retires。
retire 意为“退休”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就退休六十岁从学堂退下来，用一般过去式 retired 叙述。
retire 意为“退休”，结尾那句是母亲 1973 年的话：要退休六十岁从学堂退下来，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和集市记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 retire 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the trader retired from the school at sixty on the same day, and nobody in the market forgot it.
Even now the trader retires from the school at sixty before dawn whenever the market asks.
Retiring from the school at sixty on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever retire to the far room after supper before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new partner from the next market retires to the far room after supper on the same day every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother retired from the school at sixty again, and the market remembered that half.
